description.narrative:
In 2021 the Government of the Republic of Zimbabwe developed and adopted an integrated Formalization Strategy.
The formalization strategy was developed following a series of consultations across the Government, engaging employers, workers and informal economy associations.
The strategy includes multiple lines of action and mention ILO Recommendation No. 204. In addition, the strategy promotes coordination and coherence across a number of key institutions and policy areas. With RBSA funding, the ILO, in collaboration with UNDP, provided technical guidance for the development of the strategy. The ILO encouraged a data driven process and ensured the availability of data. It also developed the framework for consultations with workers, employers and government to ensure consensus consensus building. Lastly, ILO experts technically backstopped the work and ensured the strategy aligned with the key standards on formalization, in particular R204.
2. The strategy was based on a gender-responsive diagnostic of the informal economy that covered the characteristics, causes and circumstances of informality. The diagnostic was part of an overall Labour Market Diagnostic Assessment conducted by the ILO in preparation of the review of the National Employment Policy.

description.narrative:
In May 2021 the Government of Zimbabwe through the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and Technology - Higher Education Examinations Council (HEXCO) - accredited and registered five new training programmes under the Zimbabwe National Qualifications Framework in renewable energy and climate smart agriculture (Solar Sales and Marketing Agent; Domestic Solar PV Installation and Maintenance; Solar Agro Processing Training Package; Biogas System Installer; and Climate Smart Market Gardener). b. Qualification standards, curricula chart, skills profession schedule and training manuals were also developed as part of the process. Between April and May 2021, the ILO, through the Green enterPRIZE project funded by Sweden, provided technical support towards the consultation on curricula development, validation and adoption.
The Government of Sweden provided financial support.

description.narrative:
Through the 2020 ILO Skills Challenge Innovation Call, the Domestic Workers Association of Zimbabwe has been established as a domestic workers centre (March 2021), offering a comprehensive service package for domestic workers under one roof (soft skills, technical training, shelter for abused workers and placement services).
An innovative, flexible and inclusive skills curriculum, tailored for the domestic work sector, was developed and accredited as an official course under Higher Education Examination Council (HEXCO), recognized by the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary Education and will be offered through vocational training centers nationally. 1. The ILO through the 2020 ILO Skills Challenge Innovation Call, provided the Domestic Workers Association of Zimbabwe with a grant of USD50,000. The ILO also supported DWAZ to achieve its long-standing objective: realize decent work for domestic workers by providing them with a space to gain necessary skills to excel in their careers. DWAZ has now progressed with refined solutions, action plans and a building, where the innovation starts and flourish. DWAZ participated in the the Skills Innovation Lab to refine, prototype and develop the proposed solution. They benefitted from the participation and contributions of over 25 experts in skills development and domestic workers, as well as ILO Constituents, other UN agencies, research institutions, academic and implementing partners, local partners, and potential beneficiaries. 2. The ILO, in collaboration with the Ministry of Higher and Tertiary Education, Innovation, Science and Technology Development (Curriculum Research and Development Unit); the National Manpower Advisory Council (NAMACO); and the Domestic Workers Association of Zimbabwe (DWAZ) conducted a workshop on the development of a Curriculum for Domestic Workers in Zimbabwe (Harare, from 15 to 17 December 2020)
